_why: The golden daily.note.md fixture pins the OUTLINE format on both sides, but
it structurally cannot pin the FRONT-MATTER: its TS half round-trips
tree.frontmatter verbatim and never calls the host's touchFrontmatter, so
outline.rs's hand-rolled line-based touch_frontmatter had no counterpart
assertion at all. These cases are asserted by BOTH sides —
backend/tests/golden.rs (Rust touch_frontmatter) and
src/lib/outline/roam-golden.test.ts (host touchFrontmatter, which goes
through the `yaml` package) — so the two implementations cannot drift.
`type` is OKF v0.2's one REQUIRED key (§4.1) and the host stamps it on
every document it writes. Every case carries it, as `Daily Note`: this
plugin only ever writes <daily_dir>/<yyyy>/<yyyy-MM-dd>.note.md, which is
what the host's outlineConceptType maps to CONCEPT_TYPE.dailyNote — not the
`Outline Note` default a caller that says nothing would get. Note the
asymmetry the host's own code produces and both sides must reproduce: a
missing key is APPENDED (type, then title, then created), so `type` lands
first only on a block that had no keys at all to append after.
The `hostile title` cases at the end are the second boundary, and the
reason every case above them is deliberately NOT enough: each one uses the
title `2026-08-02`, because until incremental sync a yyyy-MM-dd date was
the only title this function ever saw. It is now the writer for arbitrary
ROAM PAGE TITLES (route.rs hands it `roam_title` verbatim), and a raw
`title: Book: Thinking Fast and Slow` is not parsable YAML at all — the
repo's own scripts/okf-lint-core.mjs calls it `frontmatter-unparsable`, and
the host's `yaml` reader swallows type/created/updated into a nested map
under `title`, after which fmHas(raw,'type') is false and the host appends
a SECOND type on its next write. `PKM #2` is quieter and worse: it parses,
so nothing complains, and the title silently becomes `PKM`. The user's own
vault already holds `wikipage/Projects- Active.note.md`, so this shape is
not hypothetical. Both sides must quote identically: the host's yaml
package decides (plain / '...' / "..."), and outline.rs's `yaml_scalar`
is a port of that decision — these cases are what holds the two together.
The three non-mapping cases are the boundary (R6). The plugin does not
have to PRODUCE such a file to be handed one: it writes into whatever daily
note is already on disk, and a .note.md is hand-edited and agent-edited
(file-over-app). Both sides leave a block that is not a YAML mapping
exactly as it was, rather than appending key: value lines to a scalar and
leaving behind front-matter the host's own reader cannot parse as a map.
The last two hostile titles are the boundary of the QUOTE STYLE itself. A
value that needs quoting, holds a `"` and no `'` takes single quotes — but a
single-quoted scalar cannot carry a raw line break in a front-matter block:
`title: 'say "hi"<LF>there'` makes the host's reader report `Missing closing
'quote`, hand back `say "hi` as the title and drop type/created/updated with
it. Unparsable front-matter, i.e. the exact failure the hostile-title cases
above exist to prevent, reached by the fix for them. So a line break always
takes the double-quoted escape form.
`host_expected` is for the ONE shape where the two writers legitimately
differ in bytes: the host's `yaml` package renders a value containing a line
break as a block scalar (`|-` plus an indented body), which outline.rs does
not re-implement (chomping indicator, indentation indicator, its own
fallbacks) for a shape no Roam page title can hold. Both are valid YAML and
the TS half asserts that BOTH byte forms read back through `parseDocument` as
the very same string — the divergence is in the spelling, never in what the
file says. Add one only with that proof; every other case has no
`host_expected` because the two sides must agree byte for byte. Note the CRLF
case immediately after: there `yaml` quotes rather than folding, so even the
bytes match, which pins that the two escape tables agree on \r and \n.
